elements.element: Renewal must occur either only by mutual written agreement or through automatic successive 12-month renewal periods.
elements.evidence: The clause states that the Agreement “may be renewed only by mutual written agreement of the parties,” satisfying the first permitted renewal structure.

elements.element: If automatic renewal is used, Customer must be able to opt out by giving 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The clause does not use automatic renewal; renewal requires mutual written agreement. The condition triggering this requirement is therefore demonstrably absent.

elements.element: If automatic renewal is used, Vendor must provide a renewal reminder 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: The clause does not use automatic renewal; renewal requires mutual written agreement. The condition triggering this reminder duty is therefore demonstrably absent.

elements.element: Any renewal price increase must be capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%.
elements.evidence: The clause provides that any renewal-period fee increase “shall not exceed the lesser of the increase in the Consumer Price Index over the preceding twelve (12) months and three percent (3%).”
The clause requires mutual written agreement for renewal and contains no automatic-renewal mechanism.

elements.element: Customer must be able to prevent automatic renewal through a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no automatic renewal and no operative Customer non-renewal notice right or notice window.

elements.element: Any renewal price increase must not exceed 5%.
elements.evidence: The lesser-of-CPI-and-3% cap cannot exceed 3%, and therefore cannot exceed 5%.

result.reason: The redline fully satisfies the preferred mutual-written-agreement route and includes the preferred price cap. The automatic-renewal-specific preferred duties are inapplicable because no automatic renewal is used. It does not satisfy the fallback because it provides neither automatic renewal nor a non-renewal notice window. The change is not strictly minimal because it adds successive 12-month renewal periods even though the mutual-written-agreement branch does not require a particular renewal duration. It otherwise preserves the termination provisions and introduces no substantive contradiction, although redundant renewal provisions and existing grammatical defects remain.
